what_it_is: Polysona v1.3.0 (MIT; shallow clone; all four releases dated 2026-03-29 for the Ralphthon Seoul hackathon) is a Claude Code plugin, a Codex skill pack and a local Bun/Hono/React dashboard whose real product is Korean social-media posts written in the user's own voice; the repository contains no tests. A persona is not an agent role but a directory personas/{id}/ of three PLOON Markdown table files about the human user: persona.md (identity layers, decision priorities, energy, blind spots, each row tagged with the psychology framework it came from, plus a dated append-only interview-log), nuance.md (register, per-platform tone/hook/emoji density, avoid/prefer phrasing) and accounts.md (rolemodel accounts, target audience profiles). Extraction is a profiler subagent prompt that interviews the human with 10 psychology frameworks and appends '~date: Framework: text' and 'GAP:' lines; the advertised structuring engine that would compile logs into tables exists nowhere, and the sample persona's log is a Korean translation of the prompt's own example block. Orchestration is the user typing /interview, /introduce, /trend, /content, /qa, /publish in order, each skill shell-preloading the files of the persona named in personas/_active.md (which nothing writes; silent 'default' fallback) and handing off through dated files under content/, so 'multi-persona' is only a directory-per-persona convention. 'Metacognition' appears only in pitch slides and can at most mean the GAP lines in which the model records contradictions between the human's self-perception layers; there is no model self-monitoring, confidence estimate or measurement. Host integration is packaging only (.claude-plugin manifests with 8 skills and 5 subagents; AGENTS.md plus a skills mirror for Codex; hooks/hooks.json whose three hooks are inert because of an invalid 'bash' type, env-var inputs and warn-only output), and the dashboard's QA and quality scores are hashes of IDs or filenames that never read the content.
architecture: Claude Code plugin manifest: registers 8 skills and 5 subagents (.claude-plugin/plugin.json:8-24)
Local marketplace: one plugin with source ./ (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:7-13)

Codex surface: AGENTS.md agent catalog and quick start; agents/openai.yaml agent-to-$skill list written for a hackathon requirement; sync script mirrors skills/ into .agents/skills/ (mirror absent at this commit although README.md:76 says it is committed) (AGENTS.md:5-47; agents/openai.yaml:1-18; scripts/sync-codex-skills.mjs:7-31)
Project instruction file: philosophy, no-speculation rules, trigger-to-mandatory-read table, PLOON conventions, pinned key facts (CLAUDE.md:5-51)

Subagent prompts: profiler (10-framework interview; maxTurns 50; memory: project), trendsetter, content-writer, virtual-follower (context: fork), admin (agents/profiler.md:1-386; agents/trendsetter.md:1-76; agents/content-writer.md:1-86; agents/virtual-follower.md:1-75; agents/admin.md:1-75)
Skills: interview, introduce, trend, content, qa, publish, status, export; most open with a !`shell` preload of the active persona's files, latest draft or directory counts (skills/*/SKILL.md:6-8)

Interview reference cards: Clean Language, Laddering+MI+ACT and McAdams question templates (skills/interview/references/clean-language.md:1-61; skills/interview/references/laddering-technique.md:1-50; skills/interview/references/mcadams-life-story.md:1-56)

Lifecycle hooks: SessionStart persona summary, PreToolUse persona-write warning, PostToolUse 'AI slop' regex; all warn-only and effectively never active (hooks/hooks.json:1-35; hooks/session-start.sh:1-22; hooks/pre-tool-use.sh:1-13; hooks/post-tool-use.sh:1-10)
Persona store: PLOON tables plus interview-log for a sample 'TestUser' (personas/default/persona.md:1-41; personas/default/nuance.md:1-24; personas/default/accounts.md:1-15)
Pipeline artifact dirs: trends, drafts, qa, published; .gitkeep only, drafts and published are gitignored (content/*/.gitkeep; .gitignore:155-158)

Dashboard API: Bun + Hono read-only JSON over personas/ and content/, PLOON parser, synthetic QA scores, hard-coded agent status (server/index.ts:1-57; server/lib/ploon.ts:1-59; server/routes/api.ts:1-218)

Dashboard UI: React 19 / Vite / Tailwind pages Home, Personas, PersonaDetail, ContentPipeline, VirtualFollower (QA), AgentMonitor (client/src/App.tsx:10-25; client/src/pages/*.tsx; client/src/components/*.tsx)

Pitch decks: 5-slide Korean and English HTML, slides-grab viewers embedding the same slides in sandboxed iframes, outlines and design notes (decks/slide-01.html:1-180; decks/viewer.html:1-1563; decks/slide-outline.md:1-61; decks/en/*)
Build config: package.json scripts (dev = vite build + bun server), tsconfig, vite root client/ (package.json:6-11; tsconfig.json:1-21; vite.config.ts:1-12)
Misc: banner recolor script with a hard-coded Windows path, MIT license, changelog (process_svg.py:1-38; LICENSE:1-21; CHANGELOG.md:1-45)

Listed, not read as content (binary or image): decks/polysona.pdf 8.58 MB and decks/en/polysona-en.pdf 8.88 MB (scanned: no object-level JavaScript/OpenAction/Launch keys); assets/banner.svg, decks/assets/banner.svg, decks/en/assets/banner.svg (byte-identical, scanned: no script); bun.lock (scanned: 166 npm packages with sha512 integrity, no git or URL sources)

atoms.name: Persona as three PLOON Markdown tables
atoms.statement: A persona is a per-user directory of three Markdown table files describing a human's identity, voice and rolemodels, pasted into prompts so generated posts sound like that person.
atoms.mechanism: persona.md holds core/decide/energy/blind tables whose rows carry a framework 'source' column plus a dated interview-log (personas/default/persona.md:5-41); nuance.md holds voice/platform/phrasing tables (personas/default/nuance.md:3-24); accounts.md holds rolemodel and virtual-audience tables (personas/default/accounts.md:3-15). The sample 'TestUser' log at personas/default/persona.md:34-41 is a translation of the prompt's example block (agents/profiler.md:375-386), not an interview result.
principle_conflict: P8: describes a human's psychology and style; proves no fact about task state or completion
PH: its purpose is to shape model output, which G1 explicitly does not do
Z2/Z4: rows are model-inferred text with an unverifiable 'source' label
atoms.g1_design: n/a

atoms.name: Ten-framework psychological interview of the user
atoms.statement: A profiler subagent elicits 'unconscious patterns' from the human with ten psychology frameworks and logs them; it is role-play interviewing with no proof-bearing purpose.
atoms.mechanism: The subagent prompt (maxTurns 50, memory: project, tools Read/Write/Bash) gives question templates for McAdams, Laddering+MI+ACT, Clean Language, Johari, IFS, Repertory Grid, Object Relations, Projective Technique, Zen Koan and 五倫+陰陽 plus a 50-minute flow (agents/profiler.md:4-9, 56-266, 326-350); AGENTS.md advertises 'defense-bypass prompts' (AGENTS.md:7).
principle_conflict: P8: interviewing a human proves no G1 fact
PH: aims to make output more 'me', not to prevent lost work or false completion
P3: relies on host subagent memory (memory: project), which is never state
Z3/Z4: framework labels and inferences are model reasoning
atoms.g1_design: n/a (the only transferable fragment, verbatim relay of source wording as in Clean Language, is covered by PSN-06)

atoms.name: Ego-layer GAP lines as 'metacognition'
atoms.statement: The only concrete referent of the advertised 'metacognition' is the model logging contradictions between five self-perception layers of the human as GAP lines; there is no model self-monitoring.
atoms.mechanism: The profiler maps answers to five layers (others-see-me, want-to-be-seen, conscious-ideal, rolemodel, unconscious-self) and must log '~date: GAP: LayerA ↔ LayerB' for any contradiction (agents/profiler.md:296-324); the dashboard splits GAP text on '↔' or ' vs ' for display (client/src/components/GapAnalysis.tsx:18-27). 'Metacognition' appears only in pitch slides (decks/slide-04.html:141, 191; decks/en/slide-04.html:142).
principle_conflict: P8: GAP lines are model-inferred prose about a human and prove nothing
Z3: contradiction detection is the model's own reasoning with no deterministic check
PH: no effect on lost work or false completion
atoms.g1_design: n/a (the transferable idea, logging declared-versus-observed contradictions, is realized deterministically as the claim-versus-receipt measurement in PSN-09)

atoms.name: Orchestration is a manual slash-command chain
atoms.statement: There is no orchestrator: the user runs commands in order, stages hand off through files, and the advertised log-to-table structuring engine is missing.
atoms.mechanism: README prescribes /interview → /introduce → /trend → /content x → /qa → /publish (README.md:90); each skill names a subagent (skills/trend/SKILL.md:4) and stages write dated files under content/ (agents/content-writer.md:20). The 'Polysona structuring engine' (AGENTS.md:22; README.md:41; agents/profiler.md:18-20) has no prompt, script or code, and the slide claim of situation-specific 'masks' (decks/en/slide-04.html:163) is unimplemented.
principle_conflict: P6: the user operates every step by hand
P8: nothing here proves a fact
Z5: architecture diagrams present an engine that does not exist
atoms.g1_design: n/a

atoms.name: Active-persona pointer with silent default fallback
atoms.statement: Every entry point resolves the active persona from personas/_active.md and silently falls back to 'default' when it is missing; nothing ever writes the pointer.
atoms.mechanism: 'cat personas/_active.md 2>/dev/null || echo default' appears in the SessionStart hook, the skill preloads and two agent prompts (hooks/session-start.sh:5-6; skills/interview/SKILL.md:7; skills/qa/SKILL.md:8; agents/content-writer.md:30; agents/trendsetter.md:27); a repo-wide search finds readers only, and the pointer text is used unsanitized as a path segment.
principle_conflict: Z7: a missing pointer silently selects a different subject instead of 'none'
P3: the selector is an unversioned, unvalidated file with no writer
atoms.g1_design: n/a (T1 rule already applies: a missing or invalid active pointer means no active task, never a default)

atoms.name: Invocation-time shell preload of on-disk state
atoms.statement: Skills run a shell command before the model sees the prompt and paste current file contents into it, so each invocation starts from on-disk state rather than conversation memory.
atoms.mechanism: Each SKILL.md opens with !`...` that cats the active persona files, the latest draft or directory counts (skills/content/SKILL.md:7; skills/qa/SKILL.md:8; skills/status/SKILL.md:6); the output is inlined into the instruction body with no delimiter or provenance. The same syntax inside a subagent prompt (agents/content-writer.md:29-30) is probably not expanded by the host.
principle_conflict: Z6/Z7: Polysona inlines raw data into the instruction channel without marking it as data
atoms.proof_purpose: the agent was shown G1's current projection (ledger head seq and hash, active contract hash) at this invocation, as recorded by G1
atoms.g1_design: PreInvocation returns one injectSteps ephemeralMessage holding a G1-computed projection (active contract id and hash, ledger head seq and hash, failing check IDs) inside an explicit data envelope with source hashes and verbatim excerpts. It is fail-open, never synthesized, and the injection grants nothing.

atoms.name: SessionStart persona summary injection hook
atoms.statement: A SessionStart hook prints the first ten lines of the active persona and four core rules, but it is declared with an invalid hook type and a relative path, so it probably never runs.
atoms.mechanism: session-start.sh prints 'head -10' of persona.md and static rules (hooks/session-start.sh:8-22); hooks.json declares it with type 'bash' and command 'bash hooks/session-start.sh' (hooks/hooks.json:4-13), whereas Claude Code's shell hook type is 'command' and the relative path only resolves when the session cwd is this repository.
principle_conflict: P4/Z7: nothing proves the hook ever fired
P8: head -10 truncation is an arbitrary projection with no proof purpose
atoms.g1_design: n/a (the SessionStart projection already exists in T1; PSN-08 covers proving hooks are live)

atoms.name: Inert advisory guard; prove hook liveness instead
atoms.statement: Polysona's only gate is a PreToolUse warning that reads environment variables the host never sets and cannot block; nobody noticed because nothing proves a hook fired, which G1 must prove every session.
atoms.mechanism: pre-tool-use.sh tests TOOL_NAME/FILE_PATH env vars and only echoes a warning with exit 0 (hooks/pre-tool-use.sh:6-13); Claude Code delivers tool input as JSON on stdin, so the condition is always false. The repo concedes host dependence without testing it (README.md:91; AGENTS.md:47).
principle_conflict: P8: keep only if some invariant depends on PreToolUse denies; otherwise the SessionStart hash check in PSN-26 suffices
atoms.proof_purpose: agy invoked G1's PreToolUse in both layers for every tool call of this conversation (the host hook contract held this session)
atoms.g1_design: Global and workspace PreToolUse hooks each append (conversationId, stepIdx, tool, sha256 of args) to G1-owned journals and print empty stdout unless denying. At Stop the agy adapter parses transcript_full.jsonl and G1 requires exact set equality between transcript tool calls and both journals, recording 'gate not live' and refusing completion on any gap.

atoms.name: Slop regex recast as claim-versus-receipt measurement
atoms.statement: A PostToolUse hook greps for sycophancy phrases (inert: wrong input channel, wrong text, warn-only); recast as a deterministic lexical detector of completion claims in the final message, it measures false completion against G1 receipts.
atoms.mechanism: post-tool-use.sh greps TOOL_OUTPUT, which the host never sets, for 'certainly|absolutely|of course|as an AI|...' and echoes a warning (hooks/post-tool-use.sh:5-10); it targets tool output, not the model's own message.
principle_conflict: Z4: must never become authority; a lexical match on model text is data, not evidence
atoms.proof_purpose: measured rate of completion claims made without a matching G1 receipt (measurement only)
atoms.g1_design: At Stop the adapter extracts the final assistant text from transcriptPath and a fixed lexical classifier flags completion claims (DONE, completed, all tests pass). G1 logs (claim, receipt_present) per Stop and reports the claim-without-receipt rate with confidence intervals across A/B variants of injected rules; it never grants or denies completion.

atoms.name: Agent write-then-read-back self-verification rule
atoms.statement: Four stages must Write a file, Read it back, then claim the saved path, and must admit failure otherwise; this is the agent verifying itself.
atoms.mechanism: Bold MUST rules in agents/admin.md:21-27, agents/content-writer.md:16-23, agents/trendsetter.md:17-24 and agents/virtual-follower.md:17-24, repeated in skills (skills/publish/SKILL.md:12-14; skills/export/SKILL.md:42); nothing outside the model checks the file.
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate (artifacts and output digests)
principle_conflict: Z5: the agent's own Read result is presented evidence
Z1: compliance with MUST is assumed
atoms.proof_purpose: none (it targets the same failure as agy's measured false DONE, but G1 already hashes artifacts itself)
atoms.g1_design: n/a (G1 computes artifact digests itself and binds them in the receipt)

atoms.name: Fresh-context evaluator as veto-only reviewer
atoms.statement: QA runs in a forked context whose inputs are only shell-preloaded files (rolemodels and latest draft), not the generator's conversation; a veto-only, artifact-fed reviewer is the only candidate for an adversarial role, and it is unproven.
atoms.mechanism: The qa skill sets context: fork and agent: virtual-follower and preloads accounts.md plus the lexically last draft (skills/qa/SKILL.md:4-8); the agent claims fork isolation keeps judgments independent of generation (agents/virtual-follower.md:4, 26-27). Its output is a positive TOP 5 ranking, not a veto, and independence was never measured.
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 3-tier hooks Stop audit with a fast judge model (partial; artifact-only fresh input is the delta)
principle_conflict: P8: a model verdict proves no fact; only a measured drop in false completion could justify it
Z1/Z4: acceptable only if PASS grants nothing
P7: needs a host model call, so it lives in the adapter
agy: a Stop timeout lets the agent stop, so the reviewer is fail-open
atoms.proof_purpose: none as authority; candidate measurable effect is a lower claim-without-receipt rate (PSN-09)
atoms.g1_design: Optional Stop-time reviewer: the adapter runs a separate fresh headless model call fed only the immutable contract and a G1-computed diff with artifact digests (never agent messages). Only an explicit FAIL citing a contract criterion ID maps to decision continue, while PASS, malformed output or timeout map to nothing; keep it only if an A/B ensemble shows a significant drop in the PSN-09 rate within agy's 10-continue bound.

atoms.name: Virtual follower persona panel scoring drafts
atoms.statement: QA role-plays demographic follower personas that score drafts on five engagement dimensions; simulated audience opinion has no proof-bearing purpose.
atoms.mechanism: Five Korean follower profiles and five dimensions (hook, empathy, share, CTA, platform fit) plus rolemodel gap analysis drive a TOP 5 recommendation (agents/virtual-follower.md:29-53); the dashboard lists 20 archetypes with age and gender (server/routes/api.ts:13-34).
principle_conflict: P8: role-played opinion proves nothing about task state
Z4: scores are model output
PH: optimizes engagement, not loss prevention
atoms.g1_design: n/a

atoms.name: Content-blind deterministic scores; require red-then-green checks
atoms.statement: The dashboard's 'deterministic' QA and quality scores are hashes of IDs or filenames that never read the content, showing that deterministic is not the same as discriminating; G1 should prove each check can fail.
atoms.mechanism: deterministicScore hashes personaId-followerId-dimension-contentName into 40..95 (server/routes/api.ts:63-72), and the qa-simulation route loads persona files only to test existence and never reads the draft (server/routes/api.ts:130-169, existence test at :139). ContentPipeline labels its five metrics 'Presentational', computed from a filename char-code sum with +15 if published (client/src/pages/ContentPipeline.tsx:56-73).
atoms.proof_purpose: each acceptance check discriminates: it fails on the pre-work tree and passes on the receipt-bound tree, so its pass is evidence of the work
atoms.g1_design: At contract admission G1 runs every acceptance check on the pre-work tree and requires failure (red); at completion the same check must pass (green) on the receipt-bound tree. A check already green before the work counts as a zero row in the coverage matrix, so the contract is rejected unless that check is declared as a regression guard.

atoms.name: Hard-coded status presented as live telemetry
atoms.statement: Agent status is the constant 'idle' with null activity and the system badge always says 'Online', so the monitor displays constants as observations.
atoms.mechanism: /agents/status returns status 'idle' and lastActivity null for every agent (server/routes/api.ts:171-193, lines 183 and 187); Home renders a static 'Online' indicator (client/src/pages/Home.tsx:56-60) under a page titled 'Background Task Orchestration' (client/src/pages/AgentMonitor.tsx:28).
principle_conflict: Z5: displayed state is fabricated
P3: status has no source fact
atoms.g1_design: n/a (lesson already in T1: every projected value cites the ledger seq and hash it derives from)

atoms.name: Substring-matched coverage vector; key on exact IDs
atoms.statement: Framework coverage n/10 is computed by substring search over the log, giving false positives and misses; G1's coverage matrix and control vector must use exact IDs.
atoms.mechanism: A framework counts as applied if its id or the first word of its name appears anywhere in the lowercased log (client/src/components/FrameworkCoverage.tsx:28-31, :83), so 'ifs' matches 'shifts' and 'zen' matches 'citizen'; timeline badges key on 'McAdams:' while logs write 'McAdams Life Story:' (client/src/components/InterviewTimeline.tsx:21-27; personas/default/persona.md:34).
atoms.proof_purpose: which contract criteria have a passing G1 receipt (exact set membership of criterion and check IDs)
atoms.g1_design: The coverage matrix and the per-turn pass/fail vector are keyed by criterion IDs from the immutable contract and check IDs in G1 receipts. Membership and Hamming distance are computed on exact ID sets, never by text search over logs or agent messages.

atoms.name: Fallback that fabricates trend evidence
atoms.statement: When live data is unavailable the trend agent is told to synthesize ranked 'trends' with 'why now' momentum reasons from the persona, and it has no web tool, so fabrication is the normal path.
atoms.mechanism: Fallback rules (agents/trendsetter.md:33, 40, 76; skills/trend/SKILL.md:14) with a required why_now field (agents/trendsetter.md:46); the agent's tools are Read/Write/Bash only (agents/trendsetter.md:4-7) while the dashboard badges it 'WebSearch' (server/routes/api.ts:38).
principle_conflict: Z5/Z7: fail-open yields invented evidence instead of absence
contradicts the repo's own no-speculation rule (CLAUDE.md:13)
atoms.g1_design: n/a (G1 fail-open means no injection or an explicit 'unknown', never synthesized content)

atoms.name: Prompt guardrails against spec-contaminated status
atoms.statement: The status skill computes counts in shell but relies on prompt rules to stop the model from filling missing state from the project spec, which documents a real failure mode without enforcing anything.
atoms.mechanism: Counts come from 'ls | wc -l' in the preload (skills/status/SKILL.md:6); guardrails forbid inferring missing frameworks from the global spec and require 'missing' over inferred completion (skills/status/SKILL.md:16-24); the changelog notes status had to be grounded in repo data (CHANGELOG.md:16).
principle_conflict: Z1: correctness depends on the model obeying the guardrail
atoms.proof_purpose: none (the failure mode 'state narrated from instructions' feeds the PSN-09 measurement)
atoms.g1_design: n/a (G1 never asks the model for status; its own projection reports 'missing' explicitly)

atoms.name: Unenforced append-only interview log
atoms.statement: The interview log is declared append-only with timestamped corrections, but enforcement is a prompt rule plus an inert warning hook, with day-granularity dates and no integrity.
atoms.mechanism: Append-only rules (agents/profiler.md:44-48, 352-357; skills/interview/SKILL.md:35), '~YYYY-MM-DD:' entries parsed by the dashboard (server/lib/ploon.ts:42-47) and a persona-write warning that never fires (hooks/pre-tool-use.sh:9-13); the Write tool replaces whole files.
principle_conflict: Z1: append-only depends on model compliance
P3: no hash chain or head anchor, so silent rewrites are undetectable
atoms.g1_design: n/a

atoms.name: Resume-first interview continuation from log
atoms.statement: A new interview reloads persona.md and resumes from the last framework and open GAP hypotheses in the log, a P1-shaped idea whose resume point the model chooses from model-written prose.
atoms.mechanism: Interview Start Protocol (skills/interview/SKILL.md:14-21) plus a mandatory read of the latest interview-log (CLAUDE.md:28).
principle_conflict: Z2/Z3: the continuation point is the model's reading of its own earlier output
P3: the log is not integrity-protected
atoms.g1_design: n/a

atoms.name: Git-as-ledger claim contradicted by gitignore
atoms.statement: The project declares git its database and history ledger while gitignoring persona directories and published content, so its canonical store is not durable by its own mechanism.
atoms.mechanism: CLAUDE.md:38-39 versus .gitignore:142-143 (personas/*/) and .gitignore:155-156 (content/drafts, content/published); the mandatory planning file sits in a gitignored and absent dir (CLAUDE.md:34; .gitignore:147).
principle_conflict: P3: durability is declared, not verified
atoms.g1_design: n/a (lesson: the durability of G1's state root is checked through the T1 head anchor, not asserted in docs)

atoms.name: Quarantine generated instructions outside host-loaded paths
atoms.statement: Persona-derived CLAUDE/AGENTS instructions go to a non-loaded generated/ folder with a review header instead of the project root; G1 needs the enforced form of this to keep agent text out of the instruction channel.
atoms.mechanism: export writes personas/{active}/generated/CLAUDE.generated.md and AGENTS.generated.md with a 'generated, review before copying into a project root' note (skills/export/SKILL.md:13-16, 26, 34, 38-42); enforcement is prompt-only and the stated goal is still to promote data into instructions (skills/export/SKILL.md:44).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 00-instinct trusted channel versus data channel (quarantine variant)
principle_conflict: P6: Polysona's promotion step is a human review; G1 must not depend on one
atoms.proof_purpose: no agent-authored bytes entered a host-loaded instruction path: at SessionStart the hashes of both hooks.json files, AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md and rule files equal the last G1-approved set
atoms.g1_design: PreToolUse denies, with a reason, agent writes to host-loaded paths such as ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json, .agents/**, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md and rule files, using tool args and best-effort parsing of sh redirections; instruction-like output may go only to a G1 quarantine dir that no loader reads. Because shell writes cannot be fully parsed, the proof is the SessionStart hash comparison against the G1-approved set.

atoms.name: Persona data promoted to standing instructions
atoms.statement: The introduce skill pastes persona files into the prompt and declares 'In this session, I am this person' for the rest of the session, turning model-written data into instructions.
atoms.mechanism: skills/introduce/SKILL.md:6-14; export converts persona fields into do-not rules for instruction files (skills/export/SKILL.md:18-26); the admin feedback loop lets the model rewrite nuance.md from engagement data (agents/admin.md:37-39), closing a data-to-instruction loop.
principle_conflict: Z6/Z7: content of unverified provenance becomes instruction
P8/PH: behavior shaping with no proof purpose
security: anything written into persona.md is injected into every later session
atoms.g1_design: n/a

atoms.name: PLOON compact table format without schema
atoms.statement: PLOON ('[table#N](cols)' plus pipe rows) is a token-compact table notation with no escaping, typing or schema, and the repo's writers, readers and data already disagree on fields.
atoms.mechanism: The parser splits rows on '|' with no quoting and names every table 'table' (server/lib/ploon.ts:26-39). Export reads a persona 'anti' field and the profiler targets 'accounts.md ideal' (skills/export/SKILL.md:25; agents/profiler.md:307), and the UI expects a voice 'mix' column (client/src/pages/PersonaDetail.tsx:88), none of which exist in the data (personas/default/persona.md:7; personas/default/nuance.md:5).
principle_conflict: P5: no canonical byte form to hash and bind
P8: compactness is not a proof purpose
atoms.g1_design: n/a (G1 keeps canonical, schema-validated, hashed JSON)

atoms.name: Trigger-to-mandatory-read context table
atoms.statement: The instruction file maps task triggers to files the model must read first, one of which is a missing, gitignored plan file that nothing checks.
atoms.mechanism: CLAUDE.md:22-34; the row at CLAUDE.md:34 points to .ref/PLAN_FOR_POLYSONA.md, which is absent and ignored by .gitignore:147.
principle_conflict: Z1: reading is left to the model
P3: pointers are not verified to exist
atoms.g1_design: n/a (lesson: any path G1 injects must be hash-verified at injection time)

atoms.name: Prompt-only invariants and no-speculation rules
atoms.statement: Agent-enforced philosophy, 'no speculation' and a pinned 'Key Facts (Must Never Be Wrong)' block live only in prose, and the repo's own Korean README already contradicts a pinned fact.
atoms.mechanism: CLAUDE.md:5-20 and CLAUDE.md:44-51 (10 frameworks, 'Not 14'), re-echoed by hooks/session-start.sh:14-19; README.ko.md:21 lists Carl Jung's persona/shadow among the ten, which the profiler's list (agents/profiler.md:56-266) does not contain.

atoms.name: Canonical source rendered into per-host mirrors
atoms.statement: Skills live once in skills/ and a script renders a Codex mirror into .agents/skills with a generated marker; the mirror the README says is committed is absent, so G1 should prove its own rendered host configuration by hash.
atoms.mechanism: sync-codex-skills.mjs deletes and recopies each skill into .agents/skills and writes .generated-by-sync (scripts/sync-codex-skills.mjs:7-8, 20-31); Claude Code gets .claude-plugin manifests and Codex gets AGENTS.md plus agents/openai.yaml (.claude-plugin/plugin.json:8-24; agents/openai.yaml:1-18). README.md:76 claims the mirror is in the repo, but .agents/ is not in the tree.
atoms.proof_purpose: the hooks.json files agy loads this session equal G1's canonical rendering (sha256 equality recorded in the ledger)
atoms.g1_design: G1 core keeps one host-neutral hook spec; the agy adapter renders ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json and .agents/hooks.json deterministically and records their sha256 in the ledger. At each SessionStart the global hook re-hashes both files and, on mismatch, injects an alert, re-renders them automatically and refuses completion for that session.

atoms.name: Dated stage artifacts with path-only provenance
atoms.statement: Each stage writes a dated Markdown file with a metadata table, and QA reports cite their source draft by path, but provenance is model-written and unhashed.
atoms.mechanism: Templates for drafts, QA and published files (agents/content-writer.md:61-86; agents/virtual-follower.md:55-75 with source_draft at :66; agents/admin.md:44-71); QA picks the lexically last filename as 'latest draft' (skills/qa/SKILL.md:8), which within one day orders by platform, not time.
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate (receipt binds artifacts and output digests)
principle_conflict: P5: a path is not a binding; content can change under it
Z2: the provenance row is written by the model
atoms.g1_design: n/a

atoms.name: Read-only local dashboard over files
atoms.statement: A Bun/Hono server exposes read-only JSON over personas/ and content/ for a React dashboard; G1 under P6 needs no UI, and this one mixes real file listings with synthetic numbers.
atoms.mechanism: GET routes for personas, interview-log, drafts, published and status (server/routes/api.ts:82-128, 195-216) are served without auth on PORT or 3000 (server/index.ts:8, 54-57); the id path parameter is interpolated into filesystem paths without validation (server/routes/api.ts:95-96).
principle_conflict: P8: no proof purpose
security: unauthenticated exposure of psychological profiles

adoption_candidates: PSN-13: red-at-admission, green-at-completion makes every G1 check provably discriminating; Polysona's content-blind 'deterministic' scores show that determinism alone proves nothing
PSN-08: per-session proof that both hook layers saw every tool call (exact set equality against the transcript); Polysona's guards were dead and nobody noticed
PSN-21: deny agent writes to host-loaded instruction and hook paths, quarantine instruction-like output, prove by SessionStart hashes (partial duplicate of the vesperchant channel split)
PSN-09: Stop-time lexical claim detector measuring the claim-without-receipt rate with confidence intervals; directly instruments agy's measured false DONE, measurement only
PSN-26: one canonical hook spec rendered per host and hash-verified at SessionStart; Polysona's generated mirror silently drifted
PSN-15: coverage matrix and control vector keyed by exact criterion and check IDs, never text search
PSN-11: research only; veto-only fresh-context reviewer fed the contract and G1 diff, kept only if an A/B ensemble shows a significant false-completion drop
PSN-06: duplicate of vesperchant/T1; PreInvocation G1-computed projection in a data envelope with source hashes
risks: Fabricated measurement: QA scores are a hash of IDs that never reads the draft, and pipeline quality metrics are a filename char-code sum, both shown as evaluation (server/routes/api.ts:63-72; server/routes/api.ts:130-169; client/src/pages/ContentPipeline.tsx:56-73); agent status and 'Online' are constants (server/routes/api.ts:183; client/src/pages/Home.tsx:59)

Sensitive personal data: the interview elicits IFS exiles, object-relations and projective material with 'defense-bypass prompts' (AGENTS.md:7; agents/profiler.md:142-245) and stores it as plaintext Markdown served by an unauthenticated dashboard (server/routes/api.ts:94-124; server/index.ts:54-57) that sets no hostname and so likely binds all interfaces under Bun's default

Prompt injection and channel mixing: persona files are inlined verbatim into skill instructions (skills/content/SKILL.md:7; skills/introduce/SKILL.md:6-14) and exported as CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rules (skills/export/SKILL.md:18-34); the admin loop lets the model rewrite nuance.md from engagement data (agents/admin.md:37-39), so injected text persists into every later session

Path handling (low): the API id parameter is interpolated into filesystem paths without validation (server/routes/api.ts:95-96; server/routes/api.ts:112-113; server/routes/api.ts:133-136) and _active.md content is used as a path segment (hooks/session-start.sh:5-6); impact is limited to reading files named persona.md, nuance.md or accounts.md

Inert controls: hooks are declared with type 'bash' and relative commands and read env vars the host does not set, and all are warn-only (hooks/hooks.json:8-9; hooks/pre-tool-use.sh:6-7; hooks/post-tool-use.sh:5)

Claims without implementation: structuring engine (AGENTS.md:22; README.md:41), committed .agents/skills mirror (README.md:76), 'metacognition' (decks/slide-04.html:141), situation masks (decks/en/slide-04.html:163), real-time trends without a web tool (agents/trendsetter.md:4-7; server/routes/api.ts:38), 'MVP LIVE' and '+50 followers' (decks/slide-05.html:175; decks/slide-03.html:170); no test files exist

Fabrication by design: the trend fallback synthesizes 'why now' trends from the persona (agents/trendsetter.md:40; agents/trendsetter.md:46) and drafts are told to use 'controversy bait' (agents/content-writer.md:41); the stated use is running AI influencer accounts at scale (decks/en/slide-outline.md:27)

Network on open: every slide and both viewers load Pretendard CSS from cdn.jsdelivr.net (decks/slide-01.html:7; decks/viewer.html:214), and README badges hit img.shields.io (README.md:8-10); no telemetry or outbound calls in server or client code

Hygiene: process_svg.py:3 hard-codes a Windows user path and the old project name 'supersona'; canonical persona and content data are gitignored despite 'git is the database' (CLAUDE.md:39; .gitignore:143; .gitignore:155-156); the mandatory planning file is missing (CLAUDE.md:34)

Low: MIT license (LICENSE:1-21); bun.lock has 166 npm packages with sha512 integrity, no git or URL sources and no install scripts; the PDFs have no object-level JavaScript/OpenAction/Launch keys (one '/AA' byte sequence lies inside a compressed stream); the SVGs contain no script; the viewers' injected slides-grab lint script cannot run because the iframes are sandboxed without allow-scripts (decks/viewer.html:129-210; decks/viewer.html:1492)

Repository instructions aimed at agents (CLAUDE.md:5-51; AGENTS.md:31-47; README.md:72-92) were treated as data; no hostile prompt-injection text aimed at analyzers was found, and no repository code was executed
